entities.text: Smt.S.Mallamma And 4 Ors vs K.Peeda Venkataiah And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This MACMA is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellants/petitioners aggrieved by the order and decree dated 19.01.2015 passed in O.P.No.2378 of 2011 by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-Cum-II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (for short "the Tribunal").
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-Cum-II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties will be hereinafter referred to as they are arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the petitioners filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- on account of the death of S. Yadaiah (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") stating that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners Nos. 2 and 4 are minor sons, petitioner No.3 is the daughter and petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased, and on 22.09.2011 at about 1.30 p.m.
the deceased and one Shiva Kumar were proceeding on Hero Honda Motorcycle bearing No.AP-28-BD-4106 from Gundlamachnoor village towards Patancheru side and when they reached Indresham village 2 RRN,J outskirts, one lorry bearing No.AP-05U-604 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner while overtaking another vehicle, dashed their motorcycle.

As a result, the deceased sustained grievous injuries to the head and other multiple injuries all over his body and immediately, he was shifted to Mythri Hospital where while undergoing treatment, succumbed to injuries on the same day at 5.00 p.m.
On a complaint, the police Patancheru registered a case in Cr.No.321 of 2011 under Section 304-A and 337 IPC against the driver of the said lorry.
It is stated that the deceased was aged about 32 years and was doing business in the name and style "Bhavani Amba Drilling Machine" at Patancheru and was getting income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
4. Before the Tribunal, respondent No.1 was set ex parte and respondent No.2 filed counter denying the petition allegations.

They mainly contended that the accident was due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle bearing No.AP- 28BD-4106 and that the owner and insurer of the said motorcycle were necessary parties and that the driver of the lorry and rider of the motorcycle were not having valid and effective driving licenses.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
3 RRN,J 5.
To prove their case, petitioners examined PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.A1 to A6.
On behalf of the respondents, neither the oral nor documentary evidence was adduced.

entities.text: Smt.S.Mallamma And 4 Ors vs K.Peeda Venkataiah And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On appreciation of the evidence on record, the Tribunal allowed the O.P. in part by awarding compensation of Rs.6,73,000/- with interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Challenging the same, the present appeal is filed by the petitioners.

7. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners inter- alia contended that the Tribunal erred in considering the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month though he was doing Drilling Machine business and did not add future prospects and that the Tribunal did not grant compensation amount under conventional heads as per the judgments of Apex Court.
Hence, prayed to allow the appeal.

8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 contended that the deceased was aged more than 40 years and since there is no evidence that the deceased was doing business and getting income, prayed to grant a reasonable amount of compensation.
4 RRN,J 9.
Heard both sides.
Perused the record.
10. A perusal of the order of the Tribunal goes to show that it considered the age of the deceased as 35 years as per Ex.A3/Inquest report and Ex.A4/PME report.
The petitioners have not filed any document to show that the deceased was doing the Drilling Machine business and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

The petitioners got filed Ex.A6/Income certificate issued by the Tahsildar,
Shivampet Mandal, which shows that the deceased was getting an annual income of Rs.50,000/-.
Even if Ex.A6 is considered, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.4,167/-.
Since it is the contention of the petitioners that the deceased was doing Drilling Machine business, it comes under creative work in nature.
Hence, this Court is inclined to fix the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.6,500/-.
To this, future prospects of 40% as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1 as the deceased was aged 26 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The annual income of the deceased including future prospects would come to Rs.1,09,200/- (Rs.6,500/- + 40%
x 12).

The appropriate multiplier as per the decision of Sarla (2017) 16 SCC 680.
5 RRN,J Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation2 is "16".

entities.text: RRN,J Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the dependants are 5 in number, a deduction of 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses which the deceased might have spent for himself.

Thus, the total loss of dependency would come to Rs.13,10,400/-
(Rs.1,09,200/- - 1/4th x 16).
11.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.5,000/- towards loss of consortium to the petitioner No.1 which are meagre.

However, the petitioners are entitled to compensation under conventional heads as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others3, and Magma Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram4.

sentences.text: Ppetitioner No.1, being the wife of the deceased, is entitled to Rs.44,000/- towards spousal consortium, petitioners No.2 and 4 being Smt.S.Mallamma And 4 Ors vs K.Peeda Venkataiah And Anr on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84736600/

entities.text: Smt.S.Mallamma And 4 Ors vs K.Peeda Venkataiah And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 minors are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each i.e. Rs.80,000/- (i.e. Rs.40,000/- x 2) towards loss of parental consortium, and petitioner No.5, being the mother of the deceased, is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards filial consortium.

The petitioners are also entitled to (2009) 6 SCC 121.
(2017) 16 SCC 680.
42018 Law Suit (SC) 904 6 RRN,J Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate.
With regard to interest, the Tribunal rightly considered at 7.5% p.a., which needs no interference.
12. In all, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to Rs.15,07,000/- towards compensation.

Though the claimed amount is Rs.10,00,000/-, invoking the principle of just compensation, and in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajesh vs. Rajbir Singh5, and in a catena of decisions, this Court is empowered to grant compensation beyond the claimed amount.

However,
the petitioner/appellant shall pay the deficit Court fee on the enhanced compensation.

13. In the result, the M.A.C.M.A is allowed and the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.6,73,000/- to Rs.15,07,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakh and seven Thousand only)
with interest @7.5 % p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Respondents No.1 and 2 are directed to deposit the said amount with costs and interest after deducting the amount, if any,
already deposited, within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this MANU/SC/0480/2013 7 RRN,J judgment.

On such deposit, the petitioners are permitted to withdraw the same in accordance with the manner and proportion as determined by the Tribunal subject to payment of deficit Court fee within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.

NAMAVARAPU RAJESHWAR RAO, J 16th day of June, 2023 BDR Smt.S.Mallamma And 4 Ors vs K.Peeda Venkataiah And Anr on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84736600/
